objective: Repair the first rejected Jen B-roll post as one coherent hook-to-caption experience grounded in the actual early-stage buyer story. Write with the clarity, rhythm, personality and conversational specificity of the approved Jen specimen. Source language is evidence; all copy is original.
output: Exactly two sections: On-screen text and Caption. One complete readable on-screen hook followed by the full conversational caption. No beat labels, reply overlay, spoken script, footage, cover, lesson template, explanation or mandatory CTA in public copy.
preserve: Approved original Jen specimen, carousels, visuals, extraction and V2 files unchanged. Keep curiosity and immediate comprehensibility together, then earn the caption payoff. Preserve actual buyer stage and source limits; no invented Jen client history.
constraints: Apply the whole feedback, not separate keyword fixes. Fifth-grade comprehension does not mean childish diction, arbitrary shortness or removing craft.

The prospective buyer is planning about ten months ahead and estimates condo versus house possibilities. Do not invent active listings, finished kitchens, listing photos, a showing or placed furniture. Illustrative language must not claim Jen observed an actual client.

The source suggests a major buying decision can carry a modest wish for an ordinary quiet evening. This is a source-backed creative interpretation, not proof of their sole motive or a universal buyer claim.

One unresolved human tension can carry the post. A property-type comparison is optional, not the assigned argument. No guarantees that detached homes are quiet, or claims about noise at an unseen condo.
Both routes receive this same frozen packet. No new external research, other-route inspection, extra agents, spending, publishing or file edits. Return complete work to the conductor.

Use the full selected methods and approved specimen as craft resources. Do not force sentence patterns, same paragraph count, mandatory model-analysis deliverables, pseudo-scientific claims, named anchors in public copy, or a different industry from the exercise onto this client assignment.

Gate A: anchor=Jen and inspected SFV buyer account; artifacts=actual thread, complete external reference, approved Jen specimen; stakes=homebuying while avoiding recurring daily frustration; mechanism=an ordinary recurring experience can define what a buyer needs a new home to change. Gate B is a separate editorial check, not human approval.

This is one bounded repair after both initial variants failed. One complete first draft per route; team editor may give one full revision contribution. No infinite optimization. Neither quality superiority nor saved human time is established.
